questions.bias_construct: Whether outcome data were available for all or nearly all randomized participants.
questions.decision_rule: Use the randomized population. For yes or probably yes, require actual outcome-availability evidence. Nearly all means missing outcomes were sufficiently few that, whatever they were, they could make no important difference; 95% often suffices for continuous outcomes, while dichotomous outcomes depend on event risk. Imputed data count as missing.
evidence_needed: For yes or probably yes, actual outcome-availability evidence can be comparable observed-outcome counts, arm-specific loss-to-follow-up or censoring accounting, or an explicit complete/nearly-complete ascertainment statement.

Compare the approved outcome/time point across participant-flow and outcome-data passages. For each comparable arm or unit distinguish randomized, observed, analysed, and imputed counts, plus exclusions and reasons. A missing count or an explicit complete-ascertainment statement is valid source information; do not substitute an analysis denominator for observed data. Calculate randomized minus observed only when population, arm, unit, and time point are the same. Imputed data count as missing.

Keep outcome availability separate from mitigation quality: a sensitivity analysis or imputation does not change the observed count, and observed cannot be inferred as analysed minus imputed unless the source establishes the same population, time window, and mutually exclusive counts.
questions.no_information_rule: Only answer no_information when the report provides no information about the extent of missing outcome data.

considerations: The appropriate population is all randomized participants, not only participants included in a final analysis. Keep outcome availability distinct from exclusions for analysis or conduct; the same passage may inform both Domains for different scientific reasons.

Distinguish administrative censoring at a common data cutoff from censoring caused by missing follow-up; inspect actual rates and follow-up accounting rather than treating a generic censoring rule as outcome-availability evidence.

For mortality, recovery or discharge does not establish vital status at a later time point. A total combining completed follow-up, recovery, and death does not establish mortality availability. mCSPC who received enzalutamide in addition to ADT
with docetaxel compared with those who did not receive
enzalutamide. However, with enzalutamide addition,
higher incidences of fatigue, syncope, and therapy
discontinuation were reported, whereas we did not
observe a rise in such events in PEACE-1 with the addition
of abiraterone to ADT with docetaxel. Aminotransferase
increase, a common side-effect of abiraterone, was
observed in this trial (6% of patients who received
abiraterone vs 1% of those who did not), but occurred at a
similar frequency with or without docetaxel. This
aminotransferase increase had no detectable clinical
consequences, as recommended management was
followed.29 Notably, the addition of abiraterone to ADT
with docetaxel did not affect severe neutropenia incidence
(10% of patients who received abiraterone vs 9% of those
who did not). The impact of toxicity on participants will
be better understood after the formal analysis of quality-
of-life data, at which time the triplet therapy oncological
benefits might still outweigh the adverse effect of the
additional toxicity.
Aside from the limitations inherently associated with
open-label trials, the rapid clinical practice evolution
for mCSPC that took place during the conduct of
this trial prompted the sequential amendment of the
PEACE-1 protocol and statistical analysis plan to reflect
those changes, answer meaningful questions, and
implement the best treatment options to all participants
(appendix pp 7-8). In particular, as an overall survival
benefit for patients with mCSPC treated with abiraterone
combined with ADT alone was shown in 2017, accrual was
then restricted to patients receiving ADT with docetaxel as
SOC, and our pre-established statistical analysis was
revised to specifically include the assessment of the
efficacy of abiraterone in terms of survival outcomes in
the ADT with docetaxel population. De facto, further
allocating men to ADT only would have been unethical,
given that the ADT plus abiraterone combination was
already known to improve overall survival.
Our findings show that combining abiraterone with
ADT and docetaxel improves both radiographic
progression-free survival and overall survival compared

sections.excerpt: ‘Nearly all’ should be interpreted as that the number of participants with missing outcome data is sufficiently small that their outcomes, whatever they were, could have made no important difference to the estimated effect of intervention. For continuous outcomes, availability of data from 95% of the participants will often be sufficient. Note that imputed data should be regarded as missing data.
sections.source_locator: Full guidance p. 45, Box 8, signalling question 3.1

sections.excerpt: Evidence that the result was not biased by missing outcome data may come from analysis methods that correct for bias, or sensitivity analyses showing that results are little changed under a range of plausible assumptions about the relationship between missingness in the outcome and its true value. However, imputing the outcome variable, either through methods such as ‘last-observation-carried-forward’ or via multiple imputation based only on intervention group, should not be assumed to correct for bias due to missing outcome data.
sections.source_locator: Full guidance p. 45, Box 8, signalling question 3.2

sections.excerpt: If loss to follow up, or withdrawal from the study, could be related to participants’ health status, then it is possible that missingness in the outcome was influenced by its true value. However, if all missing outcome data occurred for documented reasons that are unrelated to the outcome then the risk of bias due to missing outcome data will be low.
sections.source_locator: Full guidance p. 45, Box 8, signalling question 3.3

sections.excerpt: This question distinguishes between situations in which (i) missingness could depend on its true value and (ii) it is likely that missingness depended on its true value. answers.justification: The report states that survival-status data were gathered within 3 months of the cutoff date for 97% of patients. The trial profile reports 306 versus 337 alive with data from the past 3 months, 15 versus 18 alive without such data due to loss to follow-up or consent withdrawal, and 268 versus 228 deaths. Thus outcome availability was nearly complete but not universal.
unknowns: The report does not provide participant-level censoring times or a complete account of whether the small amount of unavailable status was related to prognosis.

guidance: Answer every initially active question plus each dependent question whose activation predicate is met by your earlier answers. Extra inactive branch answers are ignored and never committed. Preserve the approved Result target.

Evaluate activated questions in question order. Submit every activated question with a justification, unknowns, and counterevidence. Review the inspected passages against its exact proposition and check material contradictions. Reuse adequate Evidence. When a premise remains unresolved, state the unresolved premise and why you stopped, and use bounded discovery across relevant Sources, including a protocol or SAP when relevant. Inspect returned passages before using them. A limitation requires that explicit premise and stopping rationale; include a Trial-scoped search receipt when retrieval provenance is useful, but a direct read does not require a search receipt. Absence requires a scoped untruncated no-hit receipt.

Cite complete premises for the active question. One passage may support several facts. When an answer depends on separate passages, cite each with its own boundaries. A relationship kind describes the use of Evidence; it adds no scientific fact.

When inference, conflict, or uncertainty connects Evidence to an answer, include a concise question-specific justification. State what the passages establish, what remains unresolved, and why the selected option follows. The server checks structure and Evidence identity; you judge whether the cited facts support the answer.
A definitive yes or no needs direct_support, indirect_support, or contradiction; a limitation or absence alone supports uncertainty, not a definitive answer.

Evaluate activation against your draft answers. If validation reports missing active question IDs, add those questions with allowed answer values and supported bases, then resubmit the complete active set in one validation call. The server commits only active answers.

Apply every reported repair and retain other drafted answers. Add missing questions to the existing answer set. Resolve further activation from the repaired answers before resubmitting. The server ignores inactive answers.

traps: A no-hit search describes one lexical query, not scientific absence.
A planned method does not prove conduct; a time origin or analysis population does not prove complete follow-up or equal assessment.
An endpoint label or definition does not prove objectivity, blinding, prespecification, or no alternative analyses.

answer_anchors.text: Knowledge of intervention could influence assessment.
The outcome assessment could not be influenced by knowledge of intervention.

questions.bias_construct: Whether assessment could have been influenced by knowledge of intervention received. Keep assessor awareness separate from the mechanism by which awareness could change a judgement.
considerations: Assess whether knowledge could influence this outcome. Evidence that influence actually occurred belongs to 4.5; its absence does not resolve 4.4.

Possible influence requires a judgement or reporting pathway through which assessor awareness could matter. Awareness alone is not a measurement difference, and a susceptible outcome does not by itself show that influence was possible in this assessment.
questions.decision_rule: Knowledge could influence participant-reported outcomes, observer-reported outcomes involving judgement, and intervention-provider decisions; it is unlikely to influence observer-reported outcomes without judgement, such as all-cause mortality.
evidence_needed: Outcome type, assessor role, degree of judgement, and whether knowledge of assignment could change assessment.
invalid_shortcuts: participant blinding without identifying the outcome assessor
questions.no_information_rule: Use no_information when possible influence cannot be determined; this question is conditional on awareness in 4.3.

answer_anchors.text: Knowledge of intervention likely influenced assessment.
Knowledge could have influenced assessment but it was not likely to do so.

questions.bias_construct: Whether knowledge of intervention likely influenced outcome assessment. Require evidence or strong beliefs plus a judgement opportunity; awareness alone does not establish influence.
considerations: Possible influence without evidence it occurred maps differently from likely influence.

Likely influence requires more than assessor awareness or a possible pathway: look for evidence it occurred, or strong beliefs and a real judgement opportunity. Keep this conclusion separate from measurement susceptibility and detection opportunity.
questions.decision_rule: Distinguish possible influence without reason to believe it occurred from likely influence. Strong beliefs about benefits or harms make influence more likely, for example patient-reported symptoms in homeopathy or recovery assessed by an intervention physiotherapist.
evidence_needed: Evidence of actual influence or strong beliefs and judgement opportunities that make influence likely, given the assessor and outcome.

mCSPC who received enzalutamide in addition to ADT
with docetaxel compared with those who did not receive
enzalutamide. However, with enzalutamide addition,
higher incidences of fatigue, syncope, and therapy
discontinuation were reported, whereas we did not
observe a rise in such events in PEACE-1 with the addition

increase, a common side-effect of abiraterone, was
observed in this trial (6% of patients who received

aminotransferase increase had no detectable clinical
consequences, as recommended management was
followed.29 Notably, the addition of abiraterone to ADT
with docetaxel did not affect severe neutropenia incidence
(10% of patients who received abiraterone vs 9% of those
who did not). The impact of toxicity on participants will
be better understood after the formal analysis of quality-
of-life data, at which time the triplet therapy oncological
benefits might still outweigh the adverse effect of the
additional toxicity.
Aside from the limitations inherently associated with
open-label trials, the rapid clinical practice evolution
for mCSPC that took place during the conduct of
this trial prompted the sequential amendment of the
PEACE-1 protocol and statistical analysis plan to reflect
those changes, answer meaningful questions, and
implement the best treatment options to all participants

benefit for patients with mCSPC treated with abiraterone

efficacy of abiraterone in terms of survival outcomes in
the ADT with docetaxel population. De facto, further
allocating men to ADT only would have been unethical,
given that the ADT plus abiraterone combination was
already known to improve overall survival.

answers.justification: Overall survival was defined as time from randomisation to death from any cause, with censoring at last follow-up. This is an appropriate objective ascertainment method for an all-cause mortality endpoint.

The endpoint is all-cause death, an objective event, and survival-status data were gathered within 3 months of cutoff for 97% of patients. The trial profile reports similar small numbers without recent status data in the two groups, providing no indication that ascertainment differed between intervention groups.
unknowns: Participant-level ascertainment procedures and censoring times are not reported in full.

answers.justification: The trial was open-label, so outcome assessors could be aware of assigned intervention.

Although assignment could be known, determining whether a participant died from any cause is an objective event and is not materially susceptible to assessor interpretation in the way subjective outcomes are.

Because all-cause death is objective and the report gives no mechanism by which knowledge of treatment could alter whether death occurred or was recorded, influence of knowledge on outcome assessment is unlikely.

who did not). The impact of toxicity on participants will
be better understood after the formal analysis of quality-
of-life data, at which time the triplet therapy oncological
benefits might still outweigh the adverse effect of the
additional toxicity.
Aside from the limitations inherently associated with
open-label trials, the rapid clinical practice evolution
for mCSPC that took place during the conduct of
this trial prompted the sequential amendment of the

implement the best treatment options to all participants

Initial version of the protocol
The initial version of the protocol aimed to include n=916 men with de novo mCSPC treated with ADT alone as SOC. With
458 allocated to ADT + abiraterone (arms B and D) and 458 allocated to ADT without abiraterone (arms A and C) and a
total number of deaths of 406, a 4% level two-sided test of equal exponential survival would have an 80% power to detect a
survival difference between abiraterone-treated and abiraterone-deprived arms with a constant hazard ratio of 0.75. With the
same number of patients, and total number of 627 CRPC events, a 1% level two-sided test of equal exponential CRPC PFS
would have an 84% power to detect an improvement in PFS with a hazard ratio of 0.75. The same hypotheses were made
regarding the OS and PFS improvement related to the addition of prostate radiotherapy to systemic treatment.

5|The 2x2 factorial design of PEACE-1 offers the possibility to answer two independent questions based on different
6|hypothesis: the question of Abiraterone efficacy and the question of Radiotherapy efficacy. However, this manuscript solely
7|reports on the abiraterone question as the efficacy and safety data related to the radiotherapy question will only be analyzed
8|once the pre-planned numbers of rPFS and OS events are reached in the low-volume disease population of mCSPC men.

10|Indeed, the 2013 initial protocol planned to analyze the efficacy of abiraterone and radiotherapy simultaneously as the effect
11|of these treatments was assumed to be identical (HRABI=HRRT=0.75).
12|However, late 2018 and early 2019, the HORRAD and STAMPEDE RT trials results were published. Those trials assessed
13|the efficacy of prostate radiotherapy in the same setting than PEACE-1 (patients with de novo metastatic hormone-sensitive
14|prostate cancer treated by ADT alone as SOC). Neither, the HORRAD trial (n=432) nor the STAMPEDE RT trial (n=2061)
15|found evidence of an overall survival (OS) benefit in the overall population (HR: 0·90, 95% CI 0·70-1·14, and HR: 0·92,
16|95% CI 0·80-1·06; p=0·266, respectively) but raised the possibility that survival might be improved in a subgroup of
17|patients with low metastatic burden (HR: 0·68, 95% CI 0·42-1·10 and HR: 0·68, 95% CI 0·52-0·90; p=0·007,
18|respectively).

23|the number of events in this subgroup (299 radiographic progressions or deaths for the rPFS analysis and 213 deaths for the

25|burden. We had anticipated this situation in the protocol, which in the chapter "9.3. Interim and final analysis" p51 reads:

29|reads: "If the analysis of prostate radiotherapy and that of abiraterone are not performed at the same time, analysis of
30|abiraterone will be adjusted on radiotherapy but the HRRADIOTHERAPY will not be made public".

evidence.quote:
Since PEACE 1 initial protocol authorization on July 13TH, 2013, the treatment of men with de novo metastatic prostate
cancer has drastically evolved. Consequently, the study design and statistical analysis plan had to be adapted accordingly.
Changes to the study protocol and statistical analysis plan were made without any reference to the outcomes data collected
during the study. All amendments to the protocol were validated by the Steering committee and the Independent Data
Monitoring Committee before being submitted to dedicated regulatory authorities (depending on the country in which is
located a specific participating site) ahead of implementation. Study amendments to the protocol that affected the course of
the study and/or impacted on the study analysis are presented in an itemized fashion below (numbering and date of approval
correspond to the one validated by the French regulatory authorities).
5.1
Initial version of the protocol
The initial version of the protocol aimed to include n=916 men with de novo mCSPC treated with ADT alone as SOC. With
458 allocated to ADT + abiraterone (arms B and D) and 458 allocated to ADT without abiraterone (arms A and C) and a
total number of deaths of 406, a 4% level two-sided test of equal exponential survival would have an 80% power to detect a
survival difference between abiraterone-treated and abiraterone-deprived arms with a constant hazard ratio of 0.75. With the
same number of patients, and total number of 627 CRPC events, a 1% level two-sided test of equal exponential CRPC PFS
would have an 84% power to detect an improvement in PFS with a hazard ratio of 0.75. The same hypotheses were made
regarding the OS and PFS improvement related to the addition of prostate radiotherapy to systemic treatment.

survival (OS) and radiographic progression free survival (rPFS).
o
Assessing the efficacy of prostate radiotherapy in hormone-naïve prostate cancer patients with low
metastatic burden (as defined in the CHAARTED trial8), regardless of the SOC received (ADT with or
without docetaxel, with or without abiraterone) in terms of OS and rPFS.
•
Focus on the timing of the final analyses instead of conducting intermediate analysis based on the hypotheses
that abiraterone in the ADT+ docetaxel population would have an efficacy and that prostate radiotherapy on the
population with a low metastatic burden (in accordance with the revised primary objectives) would also have an
efficacy.
•

PSA progression had poor prognosis value as a surrogate endpoint. In contrast, rPFS was demonstrated to be a

answers.justification: The report states that eligible participants were centrally randomly assigned in a 1:1:1:1 ratio using Tenalea software and a minimisation algorithm with an 80% probability to minimise imbalance. This describes a random component in sequence generation.

Allocation was performed through the Alea Clinical Portal/Tenalea software and was solely accessed by the trial data manager until 2015, then by each investigator. This supports remote or centrally administered allocation, although the report does not fully detail access controls after the change.
unknowns: The report does not fully describe concealment safeguards after allocation access shifted to each investigator in 2015.

answers.justification: The reported randomized groups were similar in size (589 vs 583 for the assessed comparison), and the baseline table reports broadly comparable distributions across key characteristics including age, ECOG status, T stage, N stage, metastatic localization and burden, Gleason score, PSA, and medical history. No imbalance suggesting a randomization problem is apparent.
The study is explicitly described as open-label, so participants were aware of their assigned interventions.
The study is explicitly described as open-label, so investigators and intervention providers were aware of assignments.

The report states that treatments after disease progression followed common practice and investigators could change therapy based on PSA or clinical progression. These were permitted post-progression management practices, not evidence of protocol-inconsistent deviations caused by the trial context affecting the randomized assignment comparison.
unknowns: The report does not provide participant-level detail on every post-randomization treatment change.

answers.justification: Efficacy analyses were conducted in the intention-to-treat population, defined as all patients randomly assigned to a treatment group, and the reported table identifies the efficacy results as intention-to-treat analyses. This is appropriate for the effect of assignment.
unknowns: The report notes one enrolled participant withdrew consent for analysis, but does not provide participant-level reasons beyond that statement.

answers.justification: The report states that survival-status data were gathered within 3 months of the cutoff date for 97% of patients. The trial profile reports 306 versus 337 alive with data from the past 3 months, 15 versus 18 alive without such data due to loss to follow-up or consent withdrawal, and 268 versus 228 deaths. Thus outcome availability was nearly complete but not universal.
unknowns: The report does not provide participant-level censoring times or a complete account of whether the small amount of unavailable status was related to prognosis.

answers.justification: Overall survival was defined as time from randomisation to death from any cause, with censoring at last follow-up. This is an appropriate objective ascertainment method for an all-cause mortality endpoint.

The endpoint is all-cause death, an objective event, and survival-status data were gathered within 3 months of cutoff for 97% of patients. The trial profile reports similar small numbers without recent status data in the two groups, providing no indication that ascertainment differed between intervention groups.
unknowns: Participant-level ascertainment procedures and censoring times are not reported in full.

answers.justification: The trial was open-label, so outcome assessors could be aware of assigned intervention.
